answer: The protocol requires 1,000 unique credential nullifiers to authorize each autonomous AI agent, ensuring repair tasks remain distinct. An honest agent pays 1,000 computation units for these credentials, while 1,000 fake identities must expend 1,000,000 units to bypass the gate. The verifier probes the harbor of the registry for duplicate keys, uses a vault of checksums to confirm assigned repair shard integrity, and ignores any task reaching the summit without verifiable proof. Evidence of reused nullifiers triggers a permanent, non-refundable account lockout.
